Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run set for spring 2027. It will be her first full tour of the region since she stepped away from performing in 2025. She has been back onstage for months, but mostly through individual shows and festival appearances. The new dates put a multiweek run back on her calendar for the first time since the break.

The break began after she collapsed during her set at All Things Go in New York and then cancelled every remaining performance for the foreseeable future. In the message that followed, she said she needed time to work on herself and asked listeners to give her "a second chance" when she was ready to return. She set no date for coming back. The North American tour planned around *I'm Only F**king Myself* disappeared with the rest of the schedule, and there was no immediate attempt to replace it with another run.

When she did return, it happened one show at a time. "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance at the Grammys, where she also performed the song. Headline shows in Britain and festival appearances followed, including a return to All Things Go. Those dates put her back in front of large audiences without immediately committing her to another long itinerary. By the time the 2027 tour was announced, she had already spent months performing again.

[apple:song:6768357139:6768357142]

"From Down Here" arrived in May, her first new music since *I'm Only F**king Myself*. She has said the idea came the morning after the Grammys and took her into the studio with James Blake. The song is about missing an old high while knowing that a more grounded life is safer and ultimately better for her. Musically, it is calmer than much of the album, but the writing is still direct. It gives her a song from the period after the break, not just material from the album cycle that was cut short.

The tour name, "Everything Begins," reverses the wording of her "Everything Ends" tattoo. In the message cancelling her shows, she asked fans for "a second chance" when she was ready to return. She did not come back with a replacement tour. She returned through separate appearances, released new music, and only then put another full North American run on the calendar. The title belongs to that later step, when performing again becomes touring again.
